statement_record.book: The objects of a category are in bijective correspondence with its identity morphisms, an identity being uniquely characterized as a two-sided unit for composition. Consequently a category may equivalently be defined as a single collection of morphisms with a partially defined composition, certain morphisms serving both to detect composability and as two-sided identities (Ehresmann; Freyd-Scedrov).
statement_record.intree: Record object : Set := { obj_arr : arrow M; obj_def : composite M obj_arr obj_arr obj_arr; obj_id : is_identity M obj_arr } ; Program Definition Category_from_Metacategory : Category := {| obj := object; hom := morphism; ... |} ; Program Definition FromArrows (M : Metacategory) : Category := {| obj := ∃ i : arr M, identity M i; ... |}
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-weaker (one direction only). The second half of the remark is genuinely formalized twice over: Theory/Metacategory.v and Theory/Metacategory/ArrowsOnly.v both take Mac Lane's arrows-only data (a set of arrows, a partial composition given as a finite map of composable pairs, and the derived predicate `identity u` / `is_identity u` saying u is a two-sided unit) and build a full `Category` from it, with the objects DEFINED to be exactly the identity arrows (`obj := ∃ i : arr M, identity M i`, resp. `Record object` bundling `is_identity`). What is not formalized is the correspondence itself as a bijection: there is no construction taking a `Category` back to a `Metacategory`, no round-trip isomorphism, and no lemma that the identity morphisms of a category are uniquely characterized as the two-sided units (rg for id_unique / unique_id / identity_unique returns nothing).

gap: Three specific shortfalls. (1) Only the Metacategory -> Category direction exists; there is no Category -> Metacategory construction and no round trip, so the claimed BIJECTION between objects and identity morphisms is asserted only by definitional fiat (objects are defined to be identity arrows) rather than proved. The nearest thing to a round trip is the single hand-built pair Two_to_Two / Two_from_Two (Theory/Metacategory/ArrowsOnly.v:429, 508) for the two-object walking arrow. (2) No lemma states that an identity morphism of a Category is uniquely characterized as a two-sided unit for composition. (3) Theory/Metacategory.v's third axiom field `identity_law` is flagged in-file (line 184, 'jww (TODO)') as vacuously true because it uses -> where /\ was meant; the file notes this does not affect FromArrows, which reads objects off `identity` directly, but it does mean the Mac Lane axiomatization as recorded there is not faithfully constrained. statement_record.book: An ISOMORPHISM in a category is a morphism f : X -> Y for which there exists g : Y -> X with gf = id_X and fg = id_Y. Objects X and Y are ISOMORPHIC, written X ≅ Y, when some isomorphism between them exists; a morphism f is said to define an isomorphism when it is one.
